sections.h2: Where to record a document in Brevard County
sections.html:
The Clerk of Court and Comptroller runs six public offices along the county, and any of them can point you to the Recording Division. The Clerk is also the county recorder, so deeds, mortgages and liens all go into one general series of Official Records books.

Titusville400 South St., Titusville 327808 AM to 5 PM

Palm Bay450 Cogan Dr. SE, Palm Bay 32909Closed 11:30 AM to 1:30 PM
Merritt IslandAsk the Clerk for the addressClosed 11:30 AM to 1:30 PM

For mail, use P.O. Box 2767, Titusville, FL 32781-2767. The Official Records Department answers at (321) 637-2004.

The offices run from Titusville in the north through Merritt Island and Viera to Melbourne and Palm Bay in the south. Choose the one nearest your title company or your home. Titusville has two sites, South Street and the Parkway Complex, and Palm Bay and Merritt Island close over the midday stretch, so a lunchtime trip to either can fail.

The Property Appraiser is a separate elected office with its own schedule. It posts a holiday and early closure calendar on BCPAO.us, with some branch closings listed by date. Check it before driving over for an exemption question, because a Clerk visit and an appraiser visit follow different calendars.

sections.h2: Is the online Official Records search reliable?
sections.html:
Use it to find documents, and treat what you print as unofficial. The Clerk's notice on the site states that only the records held at its branch offices are the Official Public Records, and that checking accuracy is the searcher's job.

  • Try every spelling variation of a name, since the index matches what was typed at recording.
  • No password or fee is needed to search.
  • Restricted information requires a User Subscription Form for Official Records View, and a renewal fee keeps that subscription active.
  • Copies of recorded documents come only from the Clerk's office.

Sellers should know one more thing. Federal tax lien entries on the site do not match the content of what the IRS filed, so searches cannot be relied on in proceedings about title, sales or foreclosure involving a federal lien. Call (321) 637-2004 for the filed copy.

Recordable instruments include deeds, mortgages, liens, contracts, affidavits, subdivision plats, surveys, condominium declarations, bills of sale, judgments, certificates of military discharge and declarations of domicile. Recording happens on payment of statutory fees, and most of the traffic involves real estate.

That breadth explains why a title search turns up more than ownership. A Brevard parcel can show a recorded judgment against a prior owner, or a condominium declaration that governs the building, and either one can affect a sale.

sections.h2: Removing private details from the records site
sections.html:
Two Florida laws from 2021 give people a written path. A request under Chapter 2021-215 asks the Clerk to remove information exempt under sections 119.071 and 119.0714, or an image of a military discharge, a death certificate, or certain family, juvenile or probate matters. It must be notarized, state the statutory basis and confirm you qualify for the exemption.

Names in the Official Records index stay unless the name itself contains a street address, as a trust or company name might. Removal requests go to P.O. Box 2767, Titusville, FL 32781-2767, by fax at (321) 264-5246, by email to fs119exemptionrequest@brevardclerk.us, or in person at a branch.

A separate Chapter 2021-231 notice lets an affected person ask the Clerk to add the identity of a respondent in certain minor-protection injunctions, using the case number and the acclaimuseradmin@brevardclerk.us address.

The Brevard County Property Appraiser site, BCPAO.us, offers in-person help with no appointment needed. It also carries market data pages on median single-family sale prices, median market value by property type and the gap between market and assessed value, along with real property value history.

The site also links to information on Amendment 3, which covers major homestead exemption changes. Read it before you list, since exemption rules decide what a buyer inherits.

sections.h2: Recording fees and deed stamp tax
sections.html:
State statute 28.24 sets the Clerk's recording schedule per page, with small extras for added names and for trust fund and technology charges, so a longer deed costs more than a short one. Ask the Recording Division for a quote based on page count before you mail anything.

Deed stamp tax under statute 201.02 is levied on consideration, which includes any mortgage the buyer takes over. All signers share liability, and the Clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. Estate planning deeds get no special break, while a deed from a personal representative handling a probated estate is on the state's not-taxable list.

• A deed signed before two witnesses, as Florida land conveyance law requires.
  • The parcel number and legal description matching the last recorded deed.
  • Payoff letters for any mortgage or lien your search turned up.
  • The stamp tax figure and a check for the recording total, or an arrangement through the title company.
  • Proof of homestead status, if any, to share with the buyer, since a sale resets the assessed value.

Bring the originals, not copies of signatures, and ask the Recording Division whether it will accept your document before you travel to a branch.

If a deed is rejected or a release seems to be missing, call the Official Records Department at (321) 637-2004 before you resubmit. Ask what was wrong, whether a corrected page is enough, and whether the fee must be paid again. Write down the name of the person you spoke with and the date. Your title company can often fix a rejected form faster than you can, so loop them in the same day.

1. Start with the current owner's name and the parcel number from the appraiser's site.
  2. Search the Official Records under each spelling or married and maiden name, then repeat for earlier owners back to a clear chain of deeds.
  3. Note every mortgage, lien, judgment and declaration, and which have a recorded release.
  4. Order certified copies from the Clerk for anything you must rely on, because online images are unofficial.
  5. Raise a federal tax lien with the Official Records Department, since the web index can differ from what the IRS filed.

Finishing this before listing means any unreleased mortgage from an earlier owner surfaces while there is still time to ask the lender for a satisfaction. The Clerk records whatever is presented, so a missing release will not announce itself. Only the search reveals it. Keep a list of each document number you reviewed, because the title company will ask for the same references.

faqs.q: Where does Brevard County record deeds?
faqs.a: With the Clerk of Court and Comptroller, acting as county recorder, at any branch office. The Official Records Department number is (321) 637-2004.

faqs.q: Is the Brevard online records search official?
faqs.a: No. Only the records at the Clerk's branch offices are the Official Public Records, so try all spelling variations of a name and order certified copies of anything you rely on.

faqs.q: Can personal identifiers be taken off Brevard's records website?
faqs.a: Yes, for information the law makes exempt. Send a notarized written request that states the statutory basis, by mail, fax or email to the Clerk.

faqs.q: Does the Clerk's name index drop my name on request?
faqs.a: Not usually. Party names stay in the index unless the name itself contains a street address.

faqs.q: Does a Brevard deed owe documentary stamp tax?
faqs.a: Generally yes. The tax is based on consideration and every party to the document is liable. A deed signed by an estate's personal representative is on the state's list of exceptions.
